extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents/attorneys, and USPTO personnel preparing or filing Sequence Listing XML for U.S. patent applications (including national stage and international applications searched/examined by US authorities)
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and standards for preparing, formatting, submitting, and amending the Sequence Listing XML part of a patent application filed on or after July 1, 2022, in compliance with WIPO Standard ST.26 and USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum sequence length
rubrics_metrics.description: A “Sequence listing XML” must not include any sequences having fewer than 10 specifically defined nucleotides, or fewer than 4 specifically defined amino acids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit exclusion: do not list sequences below these thresholds in the Sequence Listing XML.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate listing and sequential identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Each disclosed nucleotide or amino acid sequence that meets the requirements of § 1.831(b) must appear separately in the “Sequence Listing XML.” Each sequence set forth in the “Sequence Listing XML” must be assigned a separate sequence identifier. The sequence identifiers must begin with 1 and increase sequentially by integers as defined in paragraph 10 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign SEQ ID NOs starting at 1 and increment by 1 for each listed sequence; do not combine multiple sequences under a single identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide representation format
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide sequence must be represented in the manner described in paragraphs 11–12 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow WIPO ST.26 representation rules (e.g., line length, formatting) as referenced; see ST.26 paragraphs 11–12 for exact serialization rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide symbol usage
rubrics_metrics.description: All nucleotides, including nucleotide analogs, modified nucleotides, and “unknown” nucleotides, within a nucleotide sequence must be represented using the symbols set forth in paragraphs 13–16, 19, and 21 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only the permitted symbols from WIPO ST.26 for canonical bases, ambiguous bases, modified bases, and 'unknown' residues; consult the Appendix A/B lists provided (nucleotide and modified nucleotide symbols).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified nucleotide description
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified nucleotides within a nucleotide sequence must be described in the manner discussed in paragraphs 17, 18, and 19 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the required descriptors/qualifiers for modified bases per ST.26 (see Appendix B for symbol definitions and names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint description of contiguous nucleotide residues
rubrics_metrics.description: Contiguous “a,” “c,” “g,” “t,” or “n” residues for which the same description applies may be jointly described in the manner described in paragraph 22 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use run-length or grouping notation as allowed by ST.26 paragraph 22 to compactly describe repeated residues when the same qualifiers apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino acid representation format
rubrics_metrics.description: The amino acids in an amino acid sequence must be represented in the manner described in paragraphs 24 and 25 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ST.26 rules for amino acid sequence serialization; use the specified one-letter/three-letter conventions and formatting described in the referenced paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino acid symbol usage
rubrics_metrics.description: All amino acids, including modified amino acids and 'unknown' amino acids, within an amino acid sequence must be represented using the symbols set forth in paragraphs 26–29 and 32 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the permitted amino-acid symbols from ST.26 Appendices C and D; ensure unknown/ambiguous residues use the approved symbols (e.g., Xaa, Asx, Glx).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified amino acid description
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified amino acids within an amino acid sequence must be described in the manner discussed in paragraphs 29 and 30 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide qualifiers and descriptors for modified residues per ST.26; consult Appendix D for modified/unusual amino acid symbols and meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint description of contiguous amino-acid X residues
rubrics_metrics.description: A region containing a known number of contiguous 'X' residues for which the same description applies may be jointly described in the manner described in paragraph 34 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When run(s) of unknown amino acids (X) occur and the same qualifier applies, use the ST.26 method for joint description to avoid repeating identical descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructed sequences from non-contiguous segments
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence that is constructed as a single continuous sequence derived from one or more non-contiguous segments of a larger sequence or of segments from different sequences must be listed in the “Sequence Listing XML” in the manner described in paragraph 35 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating artificial concatenations or constructs from multiple segments, follow ST.26 paragraph 35's prescribed representation to identify origins and coordinates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequences with specified residues separated by contiguous 'n' or 'X' (known counts)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence that contains regions of specifically defined residues separated by one or more regions of contiguous 'n' or 'X' residues, wherein the exact number of 'n' or 'X' residues in each region is disclosed, must be listed in the “Sequence Listing XML” in the manner described in paragraph 36 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When internal unknown stretches have known lengths, include them using the ST.26 paragraph 36 methods (i.e., specify run lengths rather than listing residues individually).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequences with gaps of unknown/undisclosed length
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence that contains regions of specifically defined residues separated by one or more gaps of an unknown or undisclosed number of residues must be listed in the “Sequence Listing XML” in the manner described in paragraph 37 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For gaps of unknown size between defined regions, use ST.26 paragraph 37 conventions to indicate unknown-length gaps rather than inventing or guessing counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing XML file encoding and character set
rubrics_metrics.description: The “Sequence Listing XML” as required by § 1.831(a) must be presented as a single file in XML 1.0 encoded using Unicode UTF–8, where the character set complies with paragraphs 40 and 41 and Annex IV of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save XML as UTF-8; ensure only permitted printable and control characters per ST.26 para 40 are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: DTD validity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sequence Listing XML' must be valid according to the Document Type Definition (DTD) as presented in WIPO Standard ST.26, Annex II.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate your XML against the ST.26 DTD (Annex II) before submission to ensure structural correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required XML elements and parts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing XML must include: (i) an XML declaration as defined in paragraph 39(a) of WIPO Standard ST.26; (ii) a document type (DOCTYPE) declaration as defined in paragraph 39(b); (iii) a root element as defined in paragraph 43; (iv) a general information part that complies with paragraphs 45, 47, and 48, as applicable; and (v) a sequence data part that complies with paragraphs 50–55, 57, 58, 60–69, 71–78, 80–87, 89–98, and 100, as applicable, of WIPO Standard ST.26 representing the nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences according to § 1.832.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all mandatory XML structural components and the general information and sequence data parts are present and conform to the referenced ST.26 paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language-dependent free-text qualifiers must have English INSDQualifier_value
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an INSDQualifier_value element with a value in English for any language-dependent free text qualifier as defined by paragraphs 76 and 85–87 of WIPO Standard ST.26, and as required by § 1.52(b)(1)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If qualifiers contain free text that depends on language, include an English-language INSDQualifier_value element in the XML (and comply with USPTO §1.52 requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: File name rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Be named as *.xml, where '*' is one character or a combination of characters limited to upper- or lowercase letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores, and the name does not exceed 60 characters in total, excluding the extension. No spaces or other types of characters are permitted in the file name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only permitted characters and length limits; do not include spaces or special characters in the filename.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer and OS compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing XML must have the following compatibilities: (i) Computer compatibility: PC or Mac®; and (ii) Operating system compatibility: MS–DOS®, MS-Windows®, Mac OS®, or Unix®/Linux®.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create files on common platforms and ensure the XML is readable on stated OSes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted characters in XML
rubrics_metrics.description: Be in XML format, where all permitted printable characters (including the space character) and nonprintable (control) characters are defined in paragraph 40 of WIPO Standard ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid characters not defined in ST.26 para 40; ensure control characters follow allowable definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission methods and file size/compression rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sequence Listing XML' must be in a single file containing the sequence information and be submitted either: (1) electronically via the USPTO patent electronic filing system, where the file size must not exceed 100 MB, and file compression is not permitted; or (2) on read-only optical disc(s) in compliance with § 1.52(e), where: (i) a file that is not compressed must be contained on a single read-only optical disc; (ii) the file may be compressed using WinZip®, 7-Zip, or Unix®/Linux® Zip; (iii) a compressed file must not be self-extracting; or (iv) a compressed XML file that does not fit on a single read-only optical disc may be split into multiple file parts, in accordance with the target read-only optical disc size, and labeled in compliance with § 1.52(e)(5)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer electronic EFS filing if under 100 MB (no compression). If using optical discs, follow the compression/software and labeling rules exactly; do not use self-extracting archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation-by-reference statement when XML submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Sequence Listing XML required by § 1.831(a) is submitted in XML file format via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or on a read-only optical disc (in compliance with § 1.52(e)), then the specification must contain a statement in a separate paragraph (see § 1.77(b)(5)) that incorporates by reference the material in the XML file identifying: (i) the name of the file; (ii) the date of creation; and (iii) the size of the file in bytes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add a separate paragraph in the specification to incorporate the XML file by reference and list the file name, creation date, and size in bytes (unless the exception for international-stage submissions applies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment requirements for adding/replacing Sequence Listing XML
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment to a patent application adding an initial submission or replacing a Sequence Listing XML after the filing date must include: (1) a Sequence Listing XML in accordance with §§ 1.831 through 1.834 submitted via EFS or on read-only optical disc; (2) a request to amend the specification to include an incorporation by reference statement identifying the name/date/size of the file (except in certain international-stage filings); (3) a statement that identifies the location of all additions, deletions, or replacements of sequence information relative to the replaced Sequence Listing XML; (4) a statement that indicates the support for the additions/deletions/replacements with specific references to particular parts of the application as originally filed (specification, claims, drawings) for all amended sequence data; and (5) a statement that the replacement Sequence Listing XML includes no new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting replacements or late additions, include the replacement XML and detailed amendment statements showing locations, support, and an explicit assertion of no new matter; label replacements 'REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' when on disc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to meet requirements — notice and opportunity to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the requirements of §§ 1.831 through 1.834 are not satisfied in an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) or in a national stage application under 35 U.S.C. 371, the applicant will be notified and given a period of time within which to comply in order to prevent abandonment of the application. Any amendment to add or replace a Sequence Listing XML or add an incorporation by reference in response to such a requirement must be submitted in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (c) of § 1.835 (with limited exceptions for translated XMLs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely respond to USPTO notices regarding Sequence Listing deficiencies; follow the amendment submission rules to avoid abandonment. Note special treatment for translated XML submissions (English translations) per paragraph (d)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: International/PCT stage compliance and late furnishing
rubrics_metrics.description: If requirements are not satisfied at the time of filing an international application under the PCT (where the application is to be searched or examined by US ISA/IPEA), the applicant may be sent a notice necessitating compliance within a prescribed time. Under PCT Rule 13ter, the applicant can provide a Sequence Listing XML in accordance with § 1.831(a). The XML must be accompanied by a statement that the information recorded does not go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. The late furnishing fee set forth in § 1.445(a)(5) is required. If the applicant fails to timely provide the required Sequence Listing XML, the US ISA/IPEA shall search/examine only to the extent a meaningful search/examination can be performed without it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international filings, supply a compliant Sequence Listing XML and required statement promptly and pay the late furnishing fee if responding to a notice; otherwise, searching and examination may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments to Sequence Listing in issued/pending patents (reissue/reexamination/correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appropriate amendments to the Sequence Listing XML in a patent (e.g., by reason of reissue, reexamination, or certificate of correction) must comply with the requirements of paragraph (b) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When amending Sequence Listing XML in post-issuance or corrective proceedings, adhere to the same representation, formatting, and submission rules that apply to initial/replacement submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: WIPO ST.26 incorporation and reference materials
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO Standard ST.26 (including Annexes I–VII, version 1.7, and as revised) is incorporated by reference for §§ 1.831 through 1.834. The WIPO Handbook and referenced ST.26 paragraphs provide the authoritative rules for presentation of nucleotide and amino acid sequence listings using XML.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use WIPO ST.26 as the primary normative standard; the MPEP cites specific ST.26 paragraphs and annexes for detailed syntax, symbol lists, feature keys, DTD, and examples. Approved IBR material is available at USPTO and NARA; contact USPTO Patent Legal Administration or WIPO as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of defined nucleotide and amino-acid symbol lists and feature keys
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices provide lists of nucleotide symbols (Appendix A), modified nucleotides (Appendix B), amino acids (Appendix C), modified/unusual amino acids (Appendix D), feature keys related to nucleotide sequences (Appendix E), and feature keys related to protein sequences (Appendix F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When populating sequence and feature fields, use the exact symbols and feature-key names from the appendices (e.g., 'a','c','g','t','n' and modified-base symbols), and use the Appendix E/F keys (e.g., CDS, gene, exon, misc_feature, MOD_RES) with their defined meanings and descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric identifier fields and formats (<110>–<230> etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The XML general information and feature sections use numeric identifiers (e.g., <110> Applicant, <120> Title of Invention, <130> File Reference, <140> Personal file reference, <151> Current Application Number, <152> Current Filing Date, <170> Prior Application Filing Date, <210> SEQ ID NO:, <211> Length, <212> Type, <213> Organism, <220> Feature, <221> Name/Key). The rule provides expected content/format (e.g., filing dates as yyyy-mm-dd, SEQ ID NO as integer, length as integer expressing bases/residues, type as DNA/RNA/PRT, organism as scientific name/Unknown/Artificial Sequence) and which fields are mandatory or optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate required numeric identifier fields using the prescribed formats and indicate mandatory (M) vs optional (O) per the appendix guidance. For <221> Name/Key, provide appropriate feature key from Appendices E/F.
